title: Honeywatch
description: SSH/Telnet honeypot activity, ingestor health and honeypot host.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: New attacker sessions in the selected time range.

panels.title: Logins
panels.description: Failed plus successful SSH/Telnet logins in the selected range.

panels.title: Success rate
panels.description: Share of login attempts that got in. Cowrie accepts some credentials on purpose, so this is a lure metric, not a health one.

panels.title: Commands
panels.description: Shell commands typed by attackers in the selected range.

panels.title: Downloads
panels.description: Files fetched or uploaded by attackers (wget, curl, scp) in the selected range.

panels.title: Countries
panels.description: Distinct source countries with at least one session in the selected range (unresolved IPs excluded).

panels.title: Ingestor
panels.description: The ingestor circuit breaker. FUSE OPEN means database writes kept failing and the ingestor stopped consuming events.

panels.title: File age
panels.description: Seconds since the ingestor last rewrote ingestor.prom. Scraped every 60s, so 0-75s is healthy; red means the ingestor or the collector is stuck.

panels.title: Sessions per hour
panels.description: New attacker sessions per hour (counters reset on ingestor restart; increase() absorbs that).

panels.title: Logins per hour: failed vs success
panels.description: A success is notable on a honeypot: an attacker got a shell. Failures are the background noise.

panels.title: Commands and downloads per hour
panels.description: Shell commands run and files transferred by attackers per hour.

panels.title: Sessions by country
panels.description: Marker size and colour scale with sessions in the selected range. Countries come from the built-in ISO alpha-2 gazetteer.

panels.title: Top 10 countries
panels.description: Sessions per source country over the selected range.

panels.title: Events processed by outcome
panels.description: Cowrie events handled per second, split by what the ingestor did with them.

panels.title: Events dropped by reason
panels.description: Events discarded without being stored. Anything above zero deserves a look.

panels.title: Parser drift by event id
panels.description: Cowrie events that failed to parse. A new non-zero series after an update means Cowrie changed a field shape.

panels.title: Fuse and consecutive write failures
panels.description: Write failures since the last success, and the circuit breaker (1 = open, ingestion halted). Both should sit at 0.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Events waiting to be written. Normally non-zero; only a steady climb is a problem.

panels.title: Dedupes, orphans, geo failures, fuse trips
panels.description: Replay dedupes, child events whose session start was missed, geo enrichment failures and breaker trips, per second.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: All cores averaged, idle time excluded.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Total minus MemAvailable, so reclaimable cache does not count as used.

panels.title: Root disk used
panels.description: Filesystem mounted at /, tmpfs and overlay excluded.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Receive above the axis, transmit below. Loopback, docker bridges and veth interfaces excluded.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Run-queue length averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes.

panels.title: Log volume by level
panels.description: Journal lines per interval, stacked by syslog level.

panels.title: Journal
panels.description: Raw systemd journal of the honeypot host, newest first, filtered by the host and unit variables.
